created_roles.name: Federal Statistics Researcher
created_roles.description: Specialist in pulling and documenting U.S. Census Bureau and BLS data. Knows the Census API, the ACS table structure and the BLS annual-average conventions. Records every figure with its exact source URL and date.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior statistical data researcher. For your assigned items, fetch values only from primary sources. ACS pattern: https://api.census.gov/data/{YEAR}/acs/acs1?get=NAME,B19013_001E,B19013_001M&for=state:18 and the same with for=us:1 for the U.S. BLS: try https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/CUUR0000SA0?startyear=2015&endyear=2023&annualaverage=true; if that fails use https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/CUUR0000SA0 or the BLS CPI tables, using the annual average (period M13 / 'Annual'). Plan your 5 turns so each fetch is one turn and leave one turn for the final table. If a fetch fails, try one alternative (web_search for the census.gov or bls.gov page) and then mark the value UNAVAILABLE with the reason; never fill from memory. Output one markdown table with columns: year | geography | value | MOE or note | source URL | data vintage | retrieved date (today's date). Mark any 2020 value 'EXPERIMENTAL (no standard release)'. Add a 2-3 line note on any limitation seen (definitions, API errors). Where the step asks for documentation points, give them as a short bulleted list with URLs.
created_roles.goal: Retrieve exact, cited ACS B19013 and CPI-U CUUR0000SA0 values for the assigned years and document why the sources fit.
responsibilities: Fetch the assigned ACS B19013_001E and B19013_001M values for Indiana (state:18) and the U.S. (us:1) from the Census API for each assigned year.
Find and fetch the 2020 experimental ACS 1-year estimate, or state it is unavailable.
Fetch CPI-U CUUR0000SA0 annual averages (M13) for 2015-2023 from BLS.
Record the URL, data vintage and retrieval date beside every number.
Collect short source documentation (ACS B19013 definition, 2020 experimental note, BLS CPI-U definition) for the fit rationale.
inputs: Assigned year(s) and geography from the step description

outputs.format: markdown table: year | geography | value | MOE or note | source URL | vintage | retrieved date

success_criteria: Every assigned value present or explicitly marked unavailable with a reason
Every row has a source URL and a date
Values come from the primary Census or BLS source, not a secondary aggregator
constraints: At most 5 turns per step, so fetch only the assigned items
Do not estimate or interpolate any value
Report 2020 as experimental, not standard

created_roles.name: Inflation-Adjustment Analyst
created_roles.description: Quantitative analyst who builds reproducible real-dollar series and publication-quality charts. Works in Python and keeps the formulas and assumptions transparent.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior quantitative analyst. You get two separate steps. CSV STEP: Turn 1: write the supplied values into a Python script (a dict per year and geography, with source URLs and the retrieved date). Turn 2: run it to compute adjusted_2023 = nominal * CPI_2023 / CPI_year, the 2015->2023 percent changes for nominal and real, and per year the Indiana/U.S. real ratio and dollar gap, from unrounded numbers. Write income_cpi_adjusted.csv with the exact required columns (one row per year x geography, plus two summary rows with year='2015-2023' per geography holding the percent changes; 2020 rows flagged EXPERIMENTAL in the note column). Turn 3: re-read the CSV and print it; check the formula with calc on two rows. Final turn: output the calculation log table, the percent-change table, a short list of assumptions, formulas and rounding rules (CPI 3 decimals, dollars to the nearest dollar, percentages 0.1 point), and the file name. CHART STEP: Turn 1: Read income_cpi_adjusted.csv. Turn 2: write and run a matplotlib script that plots only values read from the CSV: grouped bars, x = years, two bars per year (Indiana vs United States), y = real median household income in 2023 dollars. Hatch the 2020 bars and footnote them as experimental; if 2020 is unavailable, leave a gap and footnote it. Add a title containing '2023 dollars', axis labels, a legend and a source footnote with the retrieval date. Save as PNG at dpi>=150 and at least 1000 px wide. Turn 3: confirm the PNG exists and print its pixel size. Final turn: report the file name, size and a one-line description. Never fill a missing value. If your tools were not granted, say so, output the CSV text and chart script inline, and mark the PNG NOT RENDERED.
created_roles.goal: Turn the sourced data into a correct, fully documented CSV and a clear bar chart PNG, and compare Indiana with the U.S. in 2023 dollars.
responsibilities: Merge ACS and CPI tables into one dataset.
Compute adjusted 2023 dollars, the 2015-2023 percentage changes (nominal and real), and the Indiana-to-U.S. ratio and dollar gap per year, from unrounded values.
Write the CSV with citation columns and summary rows.
Record the planning record: assumptions, formulas and rounding rules used.
Produce a grouped bar chart PNG of real median household income (2023 dollars), Indiana vs U.S., 2015-2023, from the CSV.
Print the computed numbers so they can be checked.
inputs: income_cpi_adjusted.csv from step 7 (for the chart step)

outputs.format: CSV with columns year, geography, acs_nominal_usd, acs_moe_usd, cpi_u_annual_avg, adjusted_2023_usd, nominal_pct_change_2015_2023, real_pct_change_2015_2023, note, acs_source_url, cpi_source_url, retrieved_date; 18 data rows plus 2 summary rows
PNG grouped bar chart, at least 1000 px wide, titled, axes labelled, legend, source footnote
markdown table: year | geography | nominal | CPI | adjusted 2023 $ | Indiana as % of U.S. | gap $ | formula check; plus a percent-change table and a short assumptions and formulas list

The 2023 adjusted value equals the 2023 nominal value
2020 is flagged in the CSV and in the chart (hatching and footnote)
Chart has a title with '2023 dollars', labelled axes, a legend and a source footnote with retrieval date

At most 5 turns per step

created_roles.name: Independent Data Verifier
created_roles.description: Reviewer who did not produce the numbers. Re-fetches a sample from the primary sources by a different route and recomputes every derived figure.
created_roles.prompt: You are a principal engineer auditing a data deliverable you did not build. Turn 1: Read the CSV and the calculation log. Turns 2-3: re-fetch independently (try a different route than the original, e.g. a different Census endpoint or a BLS page): ACS B19013 for Indiana and the U.S. for 2015 and 2023 plus one middle year, and CPI-U CUUR0000SA0 annual average for 2015, 2023 and that middle year. Turn 4: recompute with calc/python every adjusted value and the four percentage changes; check the PNG exists, is >=1000 px wide, and that its plotted numbers come from the CSV (inspect the script or data). Check 2020 is flagged experimental and that all rows carry a URL and a date. Final turn: output a table 'item | claimed | checked | match?' and a line 'VERDICT: PASS' or 'VERDICT: FAIL' followed by the corrections needed. A mismatch beyond rounding means FAIL. responsibilities: Re-fetch at least the 2015 and 2023 ACS values for Indiana and the U.S. and the 2015 and 2023 CPI-U values, plus one middle year, from the primary sources.
Recompute all adjusted values and percentage changes with calc or python.
Check the CSV against the sourced tables and the PNG against the CSV.
Check that the 2020 treatment is flagged and that each source URL matches the claimed table or series.
inputs: CSV, PNG and calculation log from steps 7 and 8

success_criteria: At least 7 values independently re-fetched or re-derived
All derived numbers recomputed within rounding
Explicit verdict stated

Do not edit the deliverables; list corrections only
If Bash or Read is not granted, recompute with calc only and mark the PNG and CSV file checks UNVERIFIED rather than passing them

## Requirements:
R1: Open the final answer with the exact line: I read "between 2015 and 2023" as Every year from 2015 through 2023, inclusive; if you meant Only the two endpoint years, 2015 and 2023, the answer below may not apply.
R2: Compare real median household income for Indiana and the United States between 2015 and 2023, expressed in 2023 dollars: side by side for every year, with the Indiana-to-U.S. gap and the change over the period.
R3: Use the U.S. Census Bureau's American Community Survey 1-year estimates (standard release) of median household income, table B19013 (B19013_001E estimate and _001M margin of error), for Indiana and the United States for every year 2015-2023; flag 2020 as experimental-only (no standard 1-year release because of pandemic nonresponse).
R4: Use the BLS CPI-U, U.S. city average, all items, not seasonally adjusted, 1982-84=100, annual average (series CUUR0000SA0) for 2015-2023 as the inflation measure.
R5: Compute real median household income in 2023 dollars for each year and both geographies (nominal x CPI_2023 / CPI_year).
R6: Compute the percentage change from 2015 to 2023 for Indiana and the U.S., both nominal and real.
R7: Report the nominal values, the CPI-U values used, the adjusted values and the percentage changes for both geographies.
R8: Say why these sources fit (ACS B19013 and CPI-U CUUR0000SA0), including their limits: the 2020 gap, ACS margins of error, ACS values being in each survey year's dollars, national rather than Indiana-specific CPI.
R9: Deliver a CSV of the figures.
R10: Deliver a bar chart as a PNG.
R11: Cite every figure with its source and date (data vintage and retrieval date).
R12: Verify the figures, sources and calculations independently before delivery.
R13: Plan the work before staffing it: pin down the objective and deliverables, work out the numbers, and record the assumptions, formulas, rounding rules, risks and checks (the planning record) so that the deliverable states them.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Period: every year 2015 through 2023 inclusive = 2023 - 2015 + 1 = 9 calendar years (assumption fixed by the working interpretation). The standard ACS 1-year release exists for 8 of them (no standard 2020 release), so 8 x 2 = 16 standard values plus 2 experimental 2020 values = 18 data rows.
- Geographies: State of Indiana (FIPS 18, Census API for=state:18) and the United States (for=us:1).
- Income source: ACS 1-year, table B19013 'Median Household Income in the Past 12 Months (in inflation-adjusted dollars)'. The dollars are those of the survey year itself, so each year's own release is the 'nominal' figure here. Use each year's own 1-year release, not later re-adjusted comparison tables.
- Inflation source: BLS CPI-U series CUUR0000SA0, NSA, base 1982-84=100, annual average (period M13).
- Formula: adjusted_2023 = nominal_year x CPI_2023 / CPI_year. Percent change = (value_2023 / value_2015 - 1) x 100, for nominal and for real. The 2023 adjusted value equals the 2023 nominal value.
- Expected CPI-U annual averages from memory, to be verified and NOT used unless confirmed at BLS: 2015 237.017, 2016 240.007, 2017 245.120, 2018 251.107, 2019 255.657, 2020 258.811, 2021 270.970, 2022 292.655, 2023 304.702. Sanity check: 304.702 / 237.017 = 1.286, so cumulative CPI inflation 2015-2023 is about 28.6%.
- Comparison metric: Indiana real income as a percent of U.S. real income each year = Indiana adjusted / U.S. adjusted x 100, and the dollar gap = U.S. adjusted - Indiana adjusted.
- Rounding: keep CPI to 3 decimals, compute from unrounded values, show adjusted dollars to the nearest dollar and percentages to 0.1 point.
- Assumption: 2020 uses the Census experimental 2020 ACS 1-year estimates if retrievable, clearly flagged. The 2015-2023 headline change does not depend on 2020. If not retrievable, 2020 is shown as 'not available' with a note.
- Assumption: the Census API (api.census.gov/data/{year}/acs/acs1) and the BLS API or data.bls.gov are reachable through fetch_url. If not, use web_search snippets from census.gov or bls.gov pages and say so.
- Sandbox limits: each helper has at most 5 turns per step. The analyst and verifier have no network in Bash, only supplied values.

## Open Questions:
- question: How should 2020 be handled given that only experimental ACS 1-year estimates exist? | assumption: Include the experimental values, flagged, in the CSV and chart (hatched bars). If unretrievable, mark 2020 not available. The headline 2015-2023 change is unaffected.
- question: Does 'nominal' mean the ACS value as published in its own survey year's dollars? | assumption: Yes. Each year's own release is the nominal series, and we apply CPI-U ourselves to reach 2023 dollars, so there is no double adjustment.

- Inflation source: BLS CPI-U series CUUR0000SA0, NSA, 1982-84=100, annual average (period M13).
- Formula: adjusted_2023 = nominal_year x CPI_2023 / CPI_year. Percent change = (value_2023 / value_2015 - 1) x 100, for nominal and for real.

Decision point: if more than 2 values are missing, the verifier issues FAIL and steps 1-6 are re-run for the gaps.
- 2020 experimental B19013 for the state and national level may be hard to find. Decision after step 3: if missing, show 2020 as not available. The 2015-2023 headline change is unaffected.
- BLS annual-average retrieval may need an API key (v2). Fallback to BLS CPI tables or data.bls.gov; the verifier checks against a different route.
- Confusion between ACS 'inflation-adjusted dollars' and our own CPI adjustment would double-adjust. Mitigation: use each year's own release as nominal and state this explicitly.
- Later ACS vintages or the Census API may differ from originally published tables because of revisions. Mitigation: record vintage and retrieval date and report the figure as retrieved.
- Capability requests for Bash/file tools may stay unfilled. Fallbacks: the analyst emits CSV text and chart script inline marked NOT RENDERED; the verifier recomputes with calc and marks file and PNG checks UNVERIFIED; the writer says so prominently and the file-based checks cannot pass.
- Rounding differences between verifier and analyst. Mitigation: compute from unrounded values, allow rounding tolerance, fixed rounding rule in the givens.

## Requirements:
R1: Open the final answer with the exact line: I read "between 2015 and 2023" as Every year from 2015 through 2023, inclusive; if you meant Only the two endpoint years, 2015 and 2023, the answer below may not apply.
R2: Compare real median household income for Indiana and the United States between 2015 and 2023, expressed in 2023 dollars: side by side for every year, with the Indiana-to-U.S. gap and the change over the period.
R3: Use the U.S. Census Bureau's American Community Survey 1-year estimates (standard release) of median household income, table B19013 (B19013_001E estimate and _001M margin of error), for Indiana and the United States for every year 2015-2023; flag 2020 as experimental-only (no standard 1-year release because of pandemic nonresponse).
R4: Use the BLS CPI-U, U.S. city average, all items, not seasonally adjusted, 1982-84=100, annual average (series CUUR0000SA0) for 2015-2023 as the inflation measure.
R5: Compute real median household income in 2023 dollars for each year and both geographies (nominal x CPI_2023 / CPI_year).
R6: Compute the percentage change from 2015 to 2023 for Indiana and the U.S., both nominal and real.
R7: Report the nominal values, the CPI-U values used, the adjusted values and the percentage changes for both geographies.
R8: Say why these sources fit (ACS B19013 and CPI-U CUUR0000SA0), including their limits: the 2020 gap, ACS margins of error, ACS values being in each survey year's dollars, national rather than Indiana-specific CPI.
R9: Deliver a CSV of the figures.
R10: Deliver a bar chart as a PNG.
R11: Cite every figure with its source and date (data vintage and retrieval date).
R12: Verify the figures, sources and calculations independently before delivery.
R13: Plan the work before staffing it: pin down the objective and deliverables, work out the numbers, and record the assumptions, formulas, rounding rules, risks and checks (the planning record) so that the deliverable states them.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Period: every year 2015 through 2023 inclusive = 2023 - 2015 + 1 = 9 calendar years (assumption fixed by the working interpretation). The standard ACS 1-year release exists for 8 of them (no standard 2020 release), so 8 x 2 = 16 standard values plus 2 experimental 2020 values = 18 data rows.
- Geographies: State of Indiana (FIPS 18, Census API for=state:18) and the United States (for=us:1).
- Income source: ACS 1-year, table B19013 'Median Household Income in the Past 12 Months (in inflation-adjusted dollars)'. The dollars are those of the survey year itself, so each year's own release is the 'nominal' figure here. Use each year's own 1-year release, not later re-adjusted comparison tables.
- Inflation source: BLS CPI-U series CUUR0000SA0, NSA, base 1982-84=100, annual average (period M13).
- Formula: adjusted_2023 = nominal_year x CPI_2023 / CPI_year. Percent change = (value_2023 / value_2015 - 1) x 100, for nominal and for real. The 2023 adjusted value equals the 2023 nominal value.
- Expected CPI-U annual averages from memory, to be verified and NOT used unless confirmed at BLS: 2015 237.017, 2016 240.007, 2017 245.120, 2018 251.107, 2019 255.657, 2020 258.811, 2021 270.970, 2022 292.655, 2023 304.702. Sanity check: 304.702 / 237.017 = 1.286, so cumulative CPI inflation 2015-2023 is about 28.6%.
- Comparison metric: Indiana real income as a percent of U.S. real income each year = Indiana adjusted / U.S. adjusted x 100, and the dollar gap = U.S. adjusted - Indiana adjusted.
- Rounding: keep CPI to 3 decimals, compute from unrounded values, show adjusted dollars to the nearest dollar and percentages to 0.1 point.
- Assumption: 2020 uses the Census experimental 2020 ACS 1-year estimates if retrievable, clearly flagged. The 2015-2023 headline change does not depend on 2020. If not retrievable, 2020 is shown as 'not available' with a note.
- Assumption: the Census API (api.census.gov/data/{year}/acs/acs1) and the BLS API or data.bls.gov are reachable through fetch_url. If not, use web_search snippets from census.gov or bls.gov pages and say so.
- Sandbox limits: each helper has at most 5 turns per step. The analyst and verifier have no network in Bash, only supplied values.

## Open Questions:
- question: How should 2020 be handled given that only experimental ACS 1-year estimates exist? | assumption: Include the experimental values, flagged, in the CSV and chart (hatched bars). If unretrievable, mark 2020 not available. The headline 2015-2023 change is unaffected.
- question: Does 'nominal' mean the ACS value as published in its own survey year's dollars? | assumption: Yes. Each year's own release is the nominal series, and we apply CPI-U ourselves to reach 2023 dollars, so there is no double adjustment.

givens: Period: every year 2015 through 2023 inclusive = 2023 - 2015 + 1 = 9 calendar years (assumption fixed by the working interpretation). The standard ACS 1-year release exists for 8 of them (no standard 2020 release), so 8 x 2 = 16 standard values plus 2 experimental 2020 values = 18 data rows.
Geographies: State of Indiana (FIPS 18, Census API for=state:18) and the United States (for=us:1).

Income source: ACS 1-year, table B19013 'Median Household Income in the Past 12 Months (in inflation-adjusted dollars)'. The dollars are those of the survey year itself, so each year's own release is the 'nominal' figure here. Use each year's own 1-year release, not later re-adjusted comparison tables.
Inflation source: BLS CPI-U series CUUR0000SA0, NSA, base 1982-84=100, annual average (period M13).
Formula: adjusted_2023 = nominal_year x CPI_2023 / CPI_year. Percent change = (value_2023 / value_2015 - 1) x 100, for nominal and for real. The 2023 adjusted value equals the 2023 nominal value.

Expected CPI-U annual averages from memory, to be verified and NOT used unless confirmed at BLS: 2015 237.017, 2016 240.007, 2017 245.120, 2018 251.107, 2019 255.657, 2020 258.811, 2021 270.970, 2022 292.655, 2023 304.702. Comparison metric: Indiana real income as a percent of U.S. real income each year = Indiana adjusted / U.S. adjusted x 100, and the dollar gap = U.S. adjusted - Indiana adjusted.
Rounding: keep CPI to 3 decimals, compute from unrounded values, show adjusted dollars to the nearest dollar and percentages to 0.1 point.

risks: Census or BLS endpoints may be unreachable or return errors via fetch_url. Mitigation: web_search for census.gov and bls.gov pages and mark any value UNAVAILABLE rather than guessing.
